name: Mommy makeover

lead: A mommy makeover is the popular name for a package of cosmetic operations done in one session to address the changes many women see in the torso after pregnancy. The usual core is abdominoplasty (tummy tuck) plus a breast procedure such as a lift, augmentation or reduction, often with liposuction added.

The appearance payoff is a flatter, tighter midsection and a lifted or reshaped bust, aiming at the patient's pre-pregnancy contour. Published reviews and cohort studies describe high satisfaction and psychological benefit; several comparisons found complication rates similar to isolated procedures, while surgeons stress careful patient selection and operative time.

paras: Patients consult a plastic surgeon, who plans which procedures to combine based on goals and health. The operation is performed under anesthesia in a single session, followed by compression garments, a recovery period away from lifting and exercise, and follow-up visits. Surgeons describe screening for medical risk factors and limiting operative time.

Risks include those of each component procedure: seroma, hematoma, infection, wound-healing problems, scarring, asymmetry and sensation changes, plus anesthesia risks and venous thromboembolism, which surgeons treat as a central concern in combined operations. Smoking, obesity and diabetes raise risk. It is major surgery with a recovery period.

angle.text: The operations physically remove or reposition tissue, so the change in torso contour is immediate after healing. Patients and surgeons describe the goal as recovering a pre-pregnancy silhouette in one recovery period rather than several.

lead: A mommy makeover is a colloquial term for a set of cosmetic procedures performed together to reshape the body after pregnancy, most often abdominoplasty combined with breast surgery. Plastic surgeons note the phrase has entered ordinary speech because of how often this combination is requested [1][2].

People pursue it to look more like they did before childbearing: a tighter abdominal wall with less loose skin, and breasts restored in volume or position. Reviews of postpartum patients report that the abdomen and breasts are the areas most visibly changed by pregnancy and that many patients use their pre-pregnancy appearance as the benchmark for their goals [2].

Research consists mainly of surgeon case series, comparisons with single procedures and a recent meta-analysis, rather than randomized trials. Surgeons and researchers debate how combining procedures affects safety, with attention to operating time and clotting risk [1][3].
infobox: Abdominoplasty plus breast surgery, often liposuction

paras: No single standard definition exists. Reviews describe abdominoplasty as the central procedure of postpartum contouring, often supplemented with flank or mons liposuction, and breast surgery as the most common companion [2]. Abdominoplasty is among the most common cosmetic procedures in the United States, and combining it with other operations has become more common than doing it alone, with liposuction the most frequent addition followed by breast surgery, lower body lift and thigh lift [4]. Wikipedia likewise defines a mommy makeover as a breast procedure and an abdominoplasty done in one session [5].

Combining abdominoplasty with other surgery began with gynecologic and abdominal operations; as surgeons added distant procedures such as breast surgery, attention moved from wound healing to systemic risks, especially clots [1]. The marketing-friendly phrase became widespread enough that a 2010 medical ethics journal examined the 'package' [6]. An adult T Nation forum thread on improving the post-children body mentions breast implants and tummy tucks as procedures commonly called mommy makeovers [7].

In general terms, surgeons plan the combination individually, sequence the procedures and keep total duration in mind. One retrospective series describes a standardized workflow intended to improve operative efficiency in combined surgery [8], and another describes using tumescent local with spinal anesthesia as an alternative to general anesthesia [9]. Wound dressings have also been studied: a prospective study of 40 patients examined negative-pressure dressings on mommy makeover wounds [10].

A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of eight studies and 138,020 patients found no statistically significant difference in overall complications between concomitant abdominoplasty with breast surgery and isolated procedures (pooled odds ratio 1.11), though results varied widely between studies [3]. An Israeli comparison of mommy makeover procedures with abdominoplasty alone also examined complication rates [11]. A prospective Italian study of 37 women who chose either a mommy makeover or abdominoplasty alone compared satisfaction and safety questionnaires at nine months, with attention to psychological aspects [12]. A prospective 12-month study examined quality of life and psychological well-being after combined surgery in postpartum women [13], and a dyadic study examined effects on couple relationship quality and sexual wellbeing [14]. Surgeons also report onco-aesthetic variants combining DIEP flap breast reconstruction with abdominal contouring [15].

Surgeon reviews list prevention of venous thromboembolism as a paramount concern in combined procedures and recommend considering the length of surgery [1]. Wikipedia lists seroma, hematoma, infection, wound problems, necrosis, scarring and anesthesia-related events as abdominoplasty risks, with smoking, obesity, diabetes and combined procedures as risk factors [5]. Authors of the combination literature emphasize protecting patients from the added risk of prolonged operations [4].
